problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,1,4⟩,$ $b=⟨8,0,3⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,1,1⟩$ are coplanar.

examples.knowledge_point: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar
examples.problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle k,2,1 \rangle,$ $\mathbf{b}=\langle -2,-1,1 \rangle,$ and $\mathbf{c}=\langle -1,1,2 \rangle$ are coplanar.
examples.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 2 & 1 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|+1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(-1\cdot 2-1\cdot 1)-2(-2\cdot 2-(-1)\cdot 1)+(-2\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-1)) \\  & =-3k+6-3 \\  & =-3k+3.\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ -3k+3 & =0 \\ k & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=1$.

feedback.problem:
Compute the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by the vectors $x=⟨3,1,4⟩$, $y=⟨0,2,5⟩$, and $z=⟨6,0,1⟩.$

$V=${{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 5 \\ 6 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 6 & 1\end{aligned}|+4\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 6 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(2\cdot 1-5\cdot 0)-(0\cdot 1-5\cdot 6)+4(0\cdot 0-2\cdot 6) \\  & =6+30-48 \\  & =-12\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is 

$$
V=|-12|=12.
$$
